name: Blue Screen Glitch AI Trend: You, a Burning Sofa and a System Crash
blurb: Blue Screen Glitch is an AI trend that turns one photo of you into a retro computer crash: you stand still in a black suit in a dusky field, an old armchair burns behind you, error windows pop up, and a blue screen glitch flashes over everything.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 6 s, 720p, 9:16, sound on. The video prompt
prompts.text:
A retro system-crash clip in one continuous, locked-off shot with no cuts: the camera never moves. Vertical 9:16, photorealistic, cool blue dusk light and the warm glow of the fire.

The person in the clip is the person in [Image 1], in every frame: [Image 1] is the only source of their identity and look, not a style reference. Copy the exact face from [Image 1] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, skin tone, age, hair color, hair length and hairstyle, and any beard, moustache, glasses or freckles), so their friends recognize them at once. Show the whole body, from the head to the shoes. The face stays the same from the first frame to the last, also while the picture glitches; never blend it with any other face. They wear a sharp black suit with a crisp white shirt, never the clothes from [Image 1]. No sunglasses unless [Image 1] shows them. If [Image 1] shows an animal, the performer is that animal sitting upright in the same spot, with its own face, fur and markings, not a person.

The place: a wide, open green meadow at dusk with long grass, low wild bushes and a few small bare trees; behind it, a huge, broad mountain with a little snow on its peak under a cloudy, deep-blue evening sky. A few steps behind the person stands an old cream-white armchair that burns with tall orange flames and grey smoke. The person stands perfectly still in the center of the frame, in front of the burning armchair, facing the camera, arms down by the sides, with a calm, blank face.

0-1 s: stillness. Only the flames, the smoke and the grass move. The person blinks once.
1-3 s: small old-style computer error windows (plain light-grey boxes with a blue title bar, a few short lines of tiny text that cannot be read and a small OK button, laid flat over the picture like a screen overlay) pop up one after another around the person, each with a short beep. A white arrow cursor slides in and clicks one of them.
3-4 s: the whole picture glitches: horizontal tearing lines, color shifts and a short flicker. For a moment a plain blue error screen with rows of tiny white text that cannot be read flashes over the frame, and the person and the fire show through it, tinted blue.
4-6 s: the field comes back, with more error windows stacked in the corners and one bigger blue error window at the top left. The person still stands perfectly still, staring into the lens, the armchair still burning.

Audio: the crackle of the fire, a soft wind over the grass, short generic computer beeps as each window pops up, and a burst of digital glitch noise at the blue flash. No music, no voice; the person never speaks.
Exactly one person. The person never burns and never touches the fire. No logos of any kind, no flag or window logo, no brand names, no sad face on the blue screen, no readable words anywhere, no subtitles, no watermark.
